COTTONWOOD HEIGHTS CITY
PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING AGENDA
October 21, 2026

Notice is hereby given that the Cottonwood Heights Planning Commission will convene on Wednesday, October
21, 2026, at Cottonwood Heights City Hall (2277 E. Bengal Blvd., Cottonwood Heights, UT 84121) for its Work
Session and Business Session meetings.
1. Work Session – 5:00 p.m. –Council workroom
2. Business Session – 6:00 p.m. – City Council Chambers
Both sessions will also be broadcast electronically on the city’s YouTube channel at
https://www.youtube.com/@CottonwoodHeights/streams.
Please see the reverse side of this agenda for instructions on how to make public comments.
5:00 p.m. Work Session
1.0 Review Business Session Agenda
The commission will review and discuss agenda items.
2.0 CUP-25-005 -Old Mill Demolition
3.0 Adjourn
6:00 p.m. Business Session
1.0 Welcome and Acknowledgements
1.1 Ex parte communications or conflicts of interest to disclose.
2.0 General Public Comment
This is an opportunity for individuals to make general public comments that do not relate to any
projects scheduled for public hearing under the “Business Items” section of this agenda. Please see
the Public Comment Policy on the reverse side of this agenda for more information.
3.0 Business Items
3.1 Project CUP-26-020
The Planning Commission will review and take possible action on a Conditional Use Permit request
by Savana Bauer to operate childcare (The Play Lab) at 2104 East Fort Union Blvd.
3.2 Project SUB-26-005
The Planning Commission will hold a public hearing to consider a plat amendment to the South Brady
Subdivision at 2193 E. 6525 S., requested by Jordan Brady. The proposal includes adjusting the
northern boundary of Lot 203 to address an existing utility easement and considering a
recommendation to the City Council for an exception to sidewalk and curb-and-gutter requirements
under CHMC §14.12.150.
3.3 Project SUB-26-007
The Planning Commission will hold a public hearing to review and take possible action on a
subdivision plat amendment request by Jordan Brady to amend all of Lot 15 and a portion of Lot 14 of
the Ellison Woods Subdivision at 2196 E. 6450 S. The proposed amendment would establish the North

Brady Subdivision, consisting of two single-family residential lots, retaining the existing residence and
creating one additional residential building lot.
3.4 Project ZTA-26-004
The Planning Commission will hold a public hearing to review and make a possible recommendation
to the City Council on a city-initiated Zoning Text Amendment to CHMC Chapter 19.75, Accessory
Dwelling Units. The proposed amendments update ADU requirements to S.B. 284.
4.0 Consent Agenda
4.1 Approval of October 7, 2026, Planning Commission Minutes.
5.0 Adjourn
Next Scheduled Planning Commission Meeting: November 4, 2026.
Public Comment
Individuals may provide public comments verbally or via writing.
Verbal comments are accepted in person at the 6:00 p.m. Business Session, but not at the 5:00 p.m. Work Session.
At the Business Session, public comments may be given during two intervals:
1. General Public Comment Period – An opportunity for general comments not relating to specific projects on
the meeting agenda.
2. Specific Project Public Hearings – An opportunity for comments relating to specific projects on the meeting
agenda which were noticed as public hearings.
Please note that verbal comments must be provided by attending the meetings in-person. Verbal comments
cannot be provided via the electronic broadcast of planning commission meetings on the city’s YouTube channel.
Verbal comment periods are an opportunity for individuals to share comments as they see fit but are not an
opportunity for “question and answer” dialogue. Questions should be directed to city staff at
planning@ch.utah.gov. Verbal comments provided during the public comment period will be limited to three
minutes per individual, or five minutes per a spokesperson who has been asked by a group that is present to
summarize their concerns.
Alternatively, written comments may be submitted to staff via email at planning@ch.utah.gov. For written
comments to be entered into the record and distributed to the planning commission prior to the meeting, they must
be submitted to staff by 12:00 p.m. MDT on Tuesday, October 20, 2026, the day prior to the meeting. Comments
received after this deadline will be distributed to the planning commission after the meeting.
Meeting Procedures
Items will generally be considered in the following order: 1. Chair introduction of item, 2. Staff presentation, 3.
Applicant presentation, if applicable, 4. Chair opens public hearing, if applicable, 5. Chair closes public hearing, if
applicable, 6. Planning commission deliberation, 7. Planning commission motion and vote on item.
Applications may be tabled if additional information is needed in order to act on the item; or if the planning
commission feels there are unresolved issues that may need further attention before the commission is ready
to make a motion. No agenda item will begin after 9:00 pm without a unanimous vote of the commission. The
commission may carry over agenda items, scheduled late in the evening and not heard, to the next regularly
scheduled meeting.
Notice of Compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA)
In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, individuals needing special accommodations or

assistance during this meeting shall notify the City Recorder at (801) 944-7015 at least 24 hours prior to the
meeting. TDD number is (801) 270-2425 or call Relay Utah at #711.
Confirmation of Public Notice
On Thursday, October 15, 2026, a copy of the foregoing notice was posted in conspicuous view in the front
foyer of the Cottonwood Heights City Offices. The agenda was also posted on the City’s website at
www.cottonwoodheights.utah.gov and the Utah public notice website at http://pmn.utah.gov.
DATED THIS 15th DAY OF OCTOBER 2026, ATTEST: TIFFANY JANZEN, CITY RECORDER

Planning Commission Public Hearing Staff Report for CUP-26-020

Request
The applicant requests conditional use approval to operate The Play Lab, a childcare center at 2104 East
Fort Union Boulevard. The narrative describes a small childcare program with an anticipated licensed
capacity of approximately 35 children and three employees. Proposed operating hours are Monday
through Friday, 7:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. The applicant identifies five classrooms/offices, a kitchen, two
restrooms, an outdoor rear-yard play area, and an existing barn proposed for sensory and play activities.
No building reconstruction is proposed. A temporary 4 foot tall fence is proposed around the play area,
and the applicant proposes to reface the existing sign.
Staff separately confirmed with the applicant that approximately 2,000 square feet of the building
would be used for childcare activities. Staff also confirmed that the proposed business would have three
employees,

Analysis
Land use and neighborhood compatibility
A childcare/preschool is an conditional use in the NC zone. The proposed activity would occupy an existing
building, without proposed building expansion. Its daytime schedule and neighborhood-serving character
are generally consistent with the district purpose. Potential impacts associated with this particular use are
concentrated at child drop-off and pick-up times and in the rear outdoor activity area; these are addressed
below rather than presumed to be violations.

Parking and vehicle circulation
Staff evaluated the proposed childcare facility’s parking requirements using the Institute of Transportation
Engineers (ITE) Parking Generation Manual. Based on approximately 2,000 square feet of childcare space,
staff determined that five parking spaces are required for the proposed use.
The applicant’s submitted parking plan identifies three spaces designated for drop-off and pickup, one
accessible parking space, and seven additional parking spaces within the shared parking area. The
property shares parking facilities with the adjacent Brighton Dental office.
Based on the submitted parking information, the total number of available parking spaces exceeds the
five-space requirement identified through the City’s ITE parking analysis. Therefore, staff finds that the
proposed childcare facility provides sufficient parking to accommodate the anticipated parking demand,
provided that the identified spaces remain available for the proposed use.
Additionally, the applicant proposes staggered drop-off and pickup times to help manage vehicle
circulation and minimize potential traffic congestion during peak arrival and departure periods.

Planning Commission Public Hearing Staff Report for CUP-26-020

Outdoor play, accessory building, and fencing
The applicant proposes a rear-yard outdoor play area, a temporary 4 foot tall fence, and use of an existing
barn for children's activities. The proposed improvements and use of the barn shall comply with applicable
City building and fire requirements and state childcare licensing standards prior to occupancy or use.

Site improvements, access, and signage
The application states that no remodeling is proposed and includes a photograph and narrative asserting
accessible parking, an entrance ramp, and accessible interior circulation. Those representations do not
substitute for review by the responsible building or accessibility officials if a change of use, occupancy, or
required improvements triggers such review. The proposed sign reface is a separate sign-permitting
matter and must meet applicable sign requirements.
19.84.080 Determination
A. Following any public hearing, the planning commission shall consider the application in a
public meeting. The staff’s written recommendation shall be considered, among other
factors. The planning commission may either approve the proposed conditional use;
approve the proposed conditional use subject to specific modifications or conditions;
postpone decision pending consideration of additional information to be submitted by the
applicant; or deny the proposed conditional use.
B. In approving a conditional use, the planning commission may impose such requirements
and conditions as it deems necessary for the protection of adjacent properties and the public
welfare. The planning commission shall only approve with conditions, or deny a conditional
use, based upon written findings of fact with regard to each of the standards set forth below
and, where applicable, any special standards for conditional uses set forth in the specific
zoning district. The planning commission shall not approve issuance of a conditional use
permit unless the evidence presented is such as to establish the following:
1. That the proposed use is one of the conditional uses specifically listed in the zoning
district in which it is to be located;
2. That such use will not, under the circumstances of the particular case, be detrimental
to the health, safety, comfort, order or general welfare of persons residing or working
in the vicinity;
3. That the use will comply with the intent, spirit, and regulations of this title and will be
compatible with and implement the planning goals and objectives of the city;
4. That the use will be harmonious with the neighboring uses in the zoning district in
which it is to be located;
5. That nuisances which would not be in harmony with the neighboring uses, will be
abated by the conditions imposed;
6. That protection of property values, the environment, and the tax base for the city will
be assured;
7. That the use will comply with the city’s general plan;
8. That some form of a guaranty assuring compliance to all imposed conditions will be
imposed on the applicant or owner;
9. That the internal circulation system of the proposed development is properly
designed;
10. That existing and proposed utility services will be adequate for the proposed
development;
Page 5 of 7

Planning Commission Public Hearing Staff Report for CUP-26-020
October 21, 2026
11. That appropriate buffering will be provided to protect adjacent land uses from light,
noise and visual impacts;
12. That architecture and building materials are consistent with the development and
surrounding uses, and otherwise compatible with the city’s general plan, subdivision
ordinance, land use ordinance, and any applicable design standards;
13. That landscaping appropriate for the scale of the development and surrounding uses
will be installed in compliance with all applicable ordinances;
14. That the proposed use preserves historical, architectural and environmental features
of the property; and
15. That operating and delivery hours will compatible with adjacent land uses.
16. The foregoing approval standards shall be subject to any contrary requirements of
Utah Code Ann. § 10-9a-507, as amended.

Noticing
Notice of the public hearing was mailed to property owners within 300 feet of the subject property
at least 10 days prior to the public hearing, in accordance with CHMC §19.84.050.

Conclusions – Recommended Findings for Approval
1. Staff finds that the proposed childcare/preschool is a listed conditional use in the NC zoning
district and that reasonably anticipated impacts can be substantially mitigated through
reasonable conditions.
2. Based on the City's ITE parking analysis, five parking spaces are required, and the applicant
has provided sufficient parking to meet this requirement.

Recommendation
Staff recommends approval of the application with conditions:

Conditions of Approval
1. All drop-off and pickup activities shall occur on site without obstructing Fort Union Boulevard
or pedestrian access.
2. The proposed outdoor play area and fencing shall comply with applicable City regulations
and state childcare licensing requirements.
3. The existing accessory structure shall not be used for childcare activities until all applicable
building, fire, and licensing requirements have been satisfied.
4. The applicant shall obtain and maintain all required City business licenses and applicable
state childcare licenses and approvals.
5. Any proposed signage modifications shall comply with applicable City sign regulations and
obtain required permits.
6. Any substantial change or expansion of the approved use, including enrollment, staffing,
operating hours, or parking arrangements, shall be subject to applicable City review and
approval.

PLANNING COMMISSION
STAFF REPORT
October 21, 2026
Summary
Project Number:
SUB-26-005
Subject Properties:
2193 E. 6525 S.
Action Requested:
Plat Amendment
Applicant:
Jordan and Brooke Brady
Recommendation:
APPROVE WITH
CONDITIONS

Context
Property Owner:
BRADY FAM TRUST
Acreage:
Approx. 1.08 acre

Request
The applicant requests an amendment to the South Brady Subdivision involving two
modifications to the previously reviewed subdivision proposal.
The first modification would adjust the northern boundary of Lot 203 to address an existing
utility control box and associated easement serving the adjoining property to the north. The
adjustment is intended to maintain the utility facilities within an appropriate property or
easement area and prevent future conflicts regarding ownership, access, and maintenance.
The second request seeks an exception to the required sidewalk and curb-and-gutter
improvements along 6525 South, pursuant to CHMC §14.12.150.

Planning Commission – October 21, 2026
Project SUB-26-005 – 2193 E. 6525 S.

Background & Context
The Planning Commission previously reviewed the South Brady Subdivision on September
2, 2026. The subdivision proposes three single-family residential lots within approximately
1.08 acres of property identified as Lot 2 of the Brady Woods Subdivision.
The proposed lots are designated Lots 201, 202, and 203, each meeting the minimum
15,000-square-foot lot area requirement of the R-1-15 zoning district.
Following the previous Planning Commission review, the applicant continued working with
City staff and Public Works to address outstanding technical comments. During this
process, the proposed Lot 203 boundary adjustment and the request for an exception to
frontage improvements were identified.
The proposed changes do not alter the number of residential lots or the intended singlefamily residential use of the subdivision.

Analysis & Findings
1. Lot 203 Boundary Adjustment
The applicant proposes to modify the northern boundary of Lot 203 to address an existing
utility control box and associated easement benefiting the adjoining property to the north.
The proposed adjustment is intended to clarify the property boundary and ensure that the
existing utility facilities remain within an appropriate ownership or easement area. This
would help avoid potential future disputes regarding access, maintenance responsibilities,
and property rights.
Staff Analysis: Staff finds that the proposed boundary adjustment addresses an existing
site condition and supports clearer property ownership and utility access arrangements.
The modification is consistent with the overall three-lot subdivision configuration, provided
the revised lot boundaries continue to comply with applicable zoning and subdivision
requirements.
Final lot dimensions, legal descriptions, and any affected easements shall be verified
through the City's technical review process before plat recordation.
2. Exception to Sidewalk and Curb-and-Gutter Improvements
The applicant requests an exception to the sidewalk and curb-and-gutter requirements
along 6525 South.
The City's standard local street width is 56 feet, while the existing roadway corridor is
approximately 50 feet wide. The South Brady Subdivision is an infill development utilizing an
established public roadway and does not propose the construction of a new public street.
Page 2 of 6

Planning Commission – October 21, 2026
Project SUB-26-005 – 2193 E. 6525 S.
Following review of the existing roadway conditions, Public Works identified concerns
regarding the practicality of requiring standard frontage improvements at this location.
The existing street configuration includes a turnaround area near the northern end of the
roadway. Installing sidewalk, curb, and gutter along only the subdivision frontage could
result in an isolated improvement segment that does not connect effectively with the
surrounding street infrastructure.
Accommodating the standard roadway cross-section could also require additional frontage
dedication or adjustments to the existing roadway configuration, potentially affecting the
developable area of the proposed residential lots.
Applicable Code – CHMC §14.12.150, Exceptions
In cases where unusual topographical, aesthetic, or other exceptional conditions or
circumstances exist, variations or exceptions to the requirements of this chapter may be
approved by the City Council after receiving recommendations from the City's Planning
Commission and the department, provided that the variations or exceptions are not
detrimental to public safety or welfare.
Staff Analysis: Staff finds that the existing roadway width, established street configuration,
and northern turnaround present exceptional circumstances warranting consideration
under CHMC §14.12.150.
Based on Public Works' assessment, requiring standard sidewalk and curb-and-gutter
improvements along the subdivision frontage may provide limited functional benefit without
coordinated improvements to the surrounding roadway.
Staff supports the requested exception, provided the City Engineer confirms that
maintaining the existing frontage conditions will not adversely affect public safety, roadway
operations, drainage, or necessary public services.
Public work Staff will bring forward a proposed 50-foot roadway cross-section for
consideration as part of a future citywide amendment to the City's roadway design standards.

3. Subdivision Compatibility
The proposed amendment maintains the previously reviewed three-lot residential
subdivision configuration and does not introduce additional lots or a change in permitted
land use.
The Lot 203 boundary modification is intended to address existing utility infrastructure,
while the requested frontage improvement exception responds to the physical conditions of
the established roadway.

Page 3 of 6

Planning Commission – October 21, 2026
Project SUB-26-005 – 2193 E. 6525 S.
Staff Analysis: Staff finds that the proposed amendments are generally consistent with the
previously reviewed subdivision design and surrounding residential development, subject
to final verification of applicable zoning, subdivision, and engineering requirements.

Subdivision Amendment Procedure
12.26.010 Plat Vacation Process

A. The planning commission may, with or without a petition, consider any proposed
vacation, alteration, or amendment of a subdivision plat, any portion of a subdivision
plat, or any street, lot, or alley contained in a subdivision plat at a public hearing.
B. If a petition is filed, the planning commission shall hold a public hearing within 45
days after receipt of a petition.
12.26.020 Notice Of Hearing For Plat Change

A. The planning commission shall cause notice of the proposed plat change to be
mailed to each owner of real property located within 400 feet of the property that is
the subject of the proposed plat change, addressed to the owner’s mailing address
appearing on the most recent assessment rolls of the Salt Lake County Assessor.
B. The notice shall include the date, place, and time when the hearing will be held to
consider such proposed plat change.
C. If the proposed change involves the vacation, alteration, or amendment of a street,
the planning commission shall also cause notice of the date, place, and time of the
Page 4 of 6

Planning Commission – October 21, 2026
Project SUB-26-005 – 2193 E. 6525 S.
hearing regarding the matter to be given as required by UTAH CODE ANN. § 10-9a609.5, as amended.

Findings
1. The proposed second amendment maintains the three-lot single-family residential
subdivision configuration and is generally consistent with the R-1-15 zoning district,
subject to final verification of the revised lot dimensions.
2. The proposed Lot 203 boundary adjustment addresses existing utility infrastructure
and is intended to clarify property boundaries and associated easement rights.
3. The existing roadway configuration along 6525 South, including its approximately 50foot width and northern turnaround, presents exceptional circumstances warranting
consideration of an exception under CHMC §14.12.150.
4. Based on Public Works' assessment, the requested exception to sidewalk and curband-gutter improvements is appropriate, provided the City Engineer confirms that
the exception will not be detrimental to public safety or welfare.

Staff Recommendation
Staff recommend the Planning Commission:
1. Approve the proposed Lot 203 boundary adjustment, subject to final technical
review and applicable conditions of approval.
2. Forward a favorable recommendation to the City Council regarding the requested
exception to sidewalk and curb-and-gutter improvements along 6525 South
pursuant to CHMC §14.12.150.
Conditions of Approval
1. The applicant shall submit a revised subdivision plat reflecting the proposed Lot
203 boundary adjustment and demonstrate compliance with applicable zoning and
subdivision requirements.
2. All affected property boundaries, legal descriptions, utility facilities, and existing or
proposed easements shall be verified and appropriately documented before final
plat recordation.
3. The requested exception to sidewalk and curb-and-gutter improvements shall be
subject to City Council approval pursuant to CHMC §14.12.150.
4. The final frontage configuration, roadway access, and drainage requirements shall
be reviewed and approved by the City Engineer to ensure that the exception does
not adversely affect public safety or welfare.
5. The applicant shall address all remaining applicable City and agency review
comments before final plat approval and recordation.

Summary

Plat Amendment
Applicant:

Context
Property Owner:
BRADY FAM TRUST
Acreage:
Approx. 1.08 acre

Request
The applicant is requesting approval of a subdivision plat amendment to amend all of Lot 2 of the
Brady Woods Subdivision and create three single-family residential lots within the approximately
1.083-acre property.
The proposed South Brady Subdivision would establish Lot 201 at approximately 15,643 square
feet, Lot 202 at approximately 15,781 square feet, and Lot 203 at approximately 15,771 square
feet. Each proposed lot would have frontage along 6525 South and is intended for detached
single-family residential use.
The proposed plat configuration is still undergoing technical review. Planning Commission
consideration at this stage does not constitute final technical approval of the plat or construction
plans. Final plat signature and recordation will remain subject to satisfactory completion of the
City review process and resolution of all applicable staff and agency comments.

Planning Commission – September 2, 2026
Project SUB-26-005 – 2193 E. 6525 S.

Background & Context
The subject property is located along 6525 South within an established detached singlefamily residential neighborhood. The property currently consists of Lot 2 of the recorded
Brady Woods Subdivision. The proposed amendment would replace the existing lot with
three residential lots.
The applicant describes the proposal as a residential infill project intended to utilize existing
public streets and utility infrastructure while maintaining the low-density single-family
character of the surrounding neighborhood.
The submitted ALTA survey and civil plans identify existing structures, utilities, topography,
and recorded easements affecting the property. The subdivision materials also include
proposed frontage improvements, utility service connections, grading, drainage, erosioncontrol measures, and individual stormwater retention facilities.

Review Status
The South Brady Subdivision is currently undergoing technical review by City staff and
applicable reviewing agencies. Water, sewer, and Fire Department reviews have been
completed and approved. Based on the initial review, staff has not identified any major landuse or subdivision-design issues that would prevent the application from proceeding to the
Planning Commission for consideration.
Several remaining technical and drafting items are still under review and may require revisions
to the subdivision plat and associated construction documents.
Based on the review completed to date, staff does not anticipate that resolution of the
remaining comments will materially alter the basic subdivision design presented to the Planning
Commission, including the proposed three-lot configuration, general lot boundaries, lot areas,
or frontage. Any revisions that would result in a material change to the subdivision design
would be subject to additional City review, as applicable.
Planning Commission approval of the subdivision plat amendment would therefore be subject
to the applicant satisfactorily addressing all remaining staff and agency review comments prior
to final plat approval, City signatures, and recordation.

Analysis & Findings
Land Use and Zoning
The proposed subdivision would create three lots intended for detached single-family residential
development within the R-1-15 zoning district. The proposed plat identifies lot areas of 15,643
square feet, 15,781 square feet, and 15,771 square feet, each exceeding the 15,000-square-foot
minimum lot area associated with the R-1-15 district.
Page 2 of 6

Planning Commission – September 2, 2026
Project SUB-26-005 – 2193 E. 6525 S.
Staff Analysis - Staff finds that the proposed subdivision maintains detached single-family
residential use and that the proposed lot areas are consistent with the minimum lot-area
requirement of the R-1-15 district. Final verification of lot width, frontage, setbacks, and other
dimensional requirements will occur through completion of the technical review process.
The current plat includes a setback note referencing the R-1-5 zone. This reference should be
corrected to the applicable R-1-15 zoning district, together with any related setback information,
prior to final plat approval.
Plat Amendment
The proposed subdivision amends all of Lot 2 of the Brady Woods Subdivision, recorded February
25, 2005, and replaces the existing lot with three new residential lots. The submitted plat carries
forward existing utility easements and also identifies a proposed 10-foot by 10-foot well easement
benefiting an adjoining lot.
Staff Analysis - Staff finds that the proposed plat amendment is generally consistent with the
proposed three-lot subdivision configuration, subject to final verification that all existing easements,
dedications, title interests, legal descriptions, and plat references affected by the amendment are
accurately shown and legally addressed prior to recordation.
Access and Frontage Improvements
All three proposed lots would have access from 6525 South, an existing public roadway. No new
public subdivision street is proposed. The civil plans show frontage improvements along 6525 South,
including sidewalk, curb and gutter, driveway approaches, and associated utility improvements.
Staff Analysis - Staff finds that the subdivision can utilize the existing public street network. Final
frontage improvements, driveway locations, right-of-way requirements, public improvements, and
construction details remain subject to Public Works and City Engineer review and approval.
Utilities
The submitted construction plans identify existing water, sanitary sewer, gas, power, and other utility
infrastructure in the vicinity of the project and propose utility service connections for the three lots.
Staff Analysis - Water and sewer reviews have been completed and approved. Other applicable
utility and City technical requirements shall be addressed prior to final plat approval, recordation,
and/or construction authorization, as applicable.
Easements
The ALTA survey identifies recorded utility, sewer, and drainage easements affecting the property.
The proposed plat carries forward existing utility easements from the Brady Woods Subdivision and
identifies a proposed 10-foot by 10-foot well easement benefiting an adjoining lot.
Staff Analysis - All existing and proposed easements shall be verified against the applicable title
report, recorded subdivision documents, proposed lot boundaries, and utility requirements. Any
easement proposed to be created, relocated, amended, or vacated shall be properly documented
prior to plat recordation.
Drainage and Stormwater
The applicant submitted stormwater calculations identifying required retention volumes of
approximately 257 cubic feet for Lot 201 and 260 cubic feet each for Lots 202 and 203, for a total
Page 3 of 6

Planning Commission – September 2, 2026
Project SUB-26-005 – 2193 E. 6525 S.
calculated retention volume of approximately 777 cubic feet. The grading plan proposes individual
dry wells with approximately 268 cubic feet of storage per lot.
Staff Analysis - The drainage concept provides individual onsite retention for each proposed lot;
however, final grading, drainage, stormwater calculations, erosion-control measures, and dry-well
design remain subject to City Engineer review and approval through completion of the technical
review process.

Subdivision Amendment Procedure
12.26.010 Plat Vacation Process

A. The planning commission may, with or without a petition, consider any proposed vacation,
alteration, or amendment of a subdivision plat, any portion of a subdivision plat, or any
street, lot, or alley contained in a subdivision plat at a public hearing.
B. If a petition is filed, the planning commission shall hold a public hearing within 45 days after
receipt of a petition.
12.26.020 Notice Of Hearing For Plat Change
A. The planning commission shall cause notice of the proposed plat change to be mailed to
each owner of real property located within 400 feet of the property that is the subject of the
proposed plat change, addressed to the owner’s mailing address appearing on the most
recent assessment rolls of the Salt Lake County Assessor.
B. The notice shall include the date, place, and time when the hearing will be held to consider
such proposed plat change.
C. If the proposed change involves the vacation, alteration, or amendment of a street, the
planning commission shall also cause notice of the date, place, and time of the hearing
Page 4 of 6

Planning Commission – September 2, 2026
Project SUB-26-005 – 2193 E. 6525 S.
regarding the matter to be given as required by UTAH CODE ANN. § 10-9a-609.5, as
amended.

Recommendation
Based on the review completed to date, staff has not identified any significant land-use or
subdivision-design issue that would preclude approval of the proposed three-lot residential
subdivision. Water, sewer, and Fire Department reviews have been completed and approved, and
the remaining review items are primarily technical or drafting in nature and are not anticipated to
materially alter the basic subdivision configuration presented to the Planning Commission.
Staff recommends that the Planning Commission APPROVE WITH CONDITIONS the South Brady
Subdivision plat amendment, subject to completion of the remaining City technical review process
and resolution of all outstanding comments prior to recordation.
Conditions of Approval
1. Technical Review. The applicant shall address all remaining comments from Planning,
Engineering, Public Works, and other applicable reviewing agencies prior to final plat approval and
recordation.
2. Final Plat Compliance. The final plat shall comply with all applicable subdivision, zoning,
engineering, and recording requirements and shall incorporate all revisions required through the City
review process.
3. Engineering and Public Improvements. Final grading, drainage, stormwater, utility, access,
frontage, right-of-way, and public improvement requirements shall be reviewed and approved by the
City Engineer and other applicable agencies prior to final approval and/or construction, as
applicable.
4. Easements and Title. Existing and proposed easements, including the proposed well easement,
shall be verified and revised as necessary through final technical and title review prior to recordation.
Any required easement modification, vacation, relocation, or new dedication shall be properly
documented.
5. Plat Corrections. Drafting errors and inconsistencies identified during review, including zoning,
address, labeling, setback references, and other plat information, shall be corrected prior to
recording. The legal description and other survey information shall also be verified through final
technical review.
6. Utility Approvals. Water and sewer reviews have been completed and approved. The applicant
shall satisfy any remaining applicable utility-provider requirements prior to final plat recordation
and/or construction authorization, as applicable.
7. Recordation. The final plat shall be recorded within the applicable approval period established
by City Code unless an extension is approved in accordance with applicable requirements.

NOTICE TO CONTRACTOR

NOTICE TO DEVELOPER/ CONTRACTOR

ALL CONTRACTORS AND SUBCONTRACTORS PERFORMING WORK SHOWN ON OR RELATED TO THESE PLANS SHALL
CONDUCT THEIR OPERATIONS SO THAT ALL EMPLOYEES ARE PROVIDED A SAFE PLACE TO WORK AND THE PUBLIC IS
PROTECTED. ALL CONTRACTORS AND SUBCONTRACTORS SHALL COMPLY WITH THE "OCCUPATIONAL SAFETY AND HEALTH
REGULATIONS OF THE U.S. DEPARTMENT OF LABOR AND THE STATE OF UTAH DEPARTMENT OF INDUSTRIAL RELATIONS
CONSTRUCTION SAFETY ORDERS." THE CIVIL ENGINEER SHALL NOT BE RESPONSIBLE IN ANY WAY FOR THE CONTRACTORS
AND SUBCONTRACTORS COMPLIANCE WITH SAID REGULATIONS AND ORDERS.

UNAPPROVED DRAWINGS REPRESENT WORK IN PROGRESS, ARE SUBJECT TO CHANGE, AND DO NOT CONSTITUTE A
FINISHED ENGINEERING PRODUCT. ANY WORK UNDERTAKEN BY DEVELOPER OR CONTRACTOR BEFORE PLANS ARE
APPROVED IS UNDERTAKEN AT THE SOLE RISK OF THE DEVELOPER, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO BIDS, ESTIMATION,
FINANCING, BONDING, SITE CLEARING, GRADING, INFRASTRUCTURE CONSTRUCTION, ETC.

CONTRACTOR FURTHER AGREES TO ASSUME SOLE AND COMPLETE RESPONSIBILITY FOR JOB-SITE CONDITIONS DURING
THE COURSE OF CONSTRUCTION OF THIS PROJECT, INCLUDING SAFETY OF ALL PERSONS AND PROPERTY, THAT THIS
REQUIREMENT SHALL APPLY CONTINUOUSLY AND NOT BE LIMITED TO NORMAL WORKING HOURS, AND THAT THE
CONTRACTOR SHALL DEFEND, INDEMNIFY AND HOLD THE OWNER AND THE CIVIL ENGINEER HARMLESS FROM ANY AND ALL
LIABILITY, REAL OR ALLEGED IN CONNECTION WITH THE PERFORMANCE OF WORK ON THIS PROJECT, EXCEPTING FOR
LIABILITY ARISING FROM THE SOLE NEGLIGENCE OF THE OWNER OR ENGINEER.

ALL CONSTRUCTION MUST STRICTLY FOLLOW THE STANDARDS AND SPECIFICATIONS SET FORTH BY: THE DESIGN ENGINEER, LOCAL
AGENCY JURISDICTION, APWA (CURRENT EDITION), AND THE MANUAL ON UNIFORM TRAFFIC CONTROL DEVICES (M.U.T.C.D.). THE
ORDER LISTED ABOVE IS ARRANGED BY SENIORITY. THE LATEST EDITION OF ALL STANDARDS AND SPECIFICATIONS MUST BE
ADHERED TO. IF A CONSTRUCTION PRACTICE IS NOT SPECIFIED BY ANY OF THE LISTED SOURCES, CONTRACTOR MUST CONTACT
DESIGN ENGINEER FOR DIRECTION.

1.

1.

CONTRACTOR TO STRICTLY FOLLOW THE MOST CURRENT COPY OF THE SOILS REPORT FOR THIS PROJECT. ALL GRADING
INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO CUT, FILL, COMPACTION, ASPHALT SECTION, SUBBASE, TRENCH EXCAVATION/BACKFILL, SITE
GRUBBING, AND FOOTINGS MUST BE COORDINATED DIRECTLY WITH SOILS REPORT.

2.

2.

3.
3.
4.

CONTRACTOR MUST VERIFY ALL EXISTING CONDITIONS BEFORE BIDDING, AND BRING UP ANY QUESTIONS BEFORE SUBMITTING BID.
CONTRACTOR SHALL PROVIDE A CONSTRUCTION SCHEDULE IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE CITY, STATE, OR COUNTY REGULATIONS FOR
WORKING IN THE PUBLIC WAY.

5.

CONTRACTOR SHALL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR DUST CONTROL ACCORDING TO GOVERNING AGENCY STANDARDS. WET DOWN DRY
MATERIALS AND RUBBISH TO PREVENT BLOWING.

6.

CONTRACTOR SHALL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR ANY DAMAGE TO ADJACENT SURFACE IMPROVEMENTS.

7.
8.
9.

10.

CONTRACTOR SHALL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR CORRECTING ANY SETTLEMENT OF OR DAMAGE TO EXISTING UTILITIES.

4.

THE CONTRACTOR IS RESPONSIBLE TO FURNISH ALL MATERIALS TO COMPLETE THE PROJECT.
ALL EXPOSED SURFACES WILL HAVE A TEXTURED FINISH, RUBBED, OR BROOMED. ANY "PLASTERING" OF NEW CONCRETE WILL BE
DONE WHILE IT IS STILL "GREEN".

12.

13.

14.

15.

ALL DIMENSIONS, GRADES, AND UTILITY DESIGN SHOWN ON THE PLANS SHALL BE VERIFIED BY THE CONTRACTOR PRIOR TO
CONSTRUCTION. CONTRACTOR SHALL NOTIFY THE ENGINEER IF ANY DISCREPANCIES EXIST, PRIOR TO PROCEEDING WITH
CONSTRUCTION FOR NECESSARY PLAN OR GRADE CHANGES. NO EXTRA COMPENSATION SHALL BE PAID TO THE CONTRACTOR FOR
WORK HAVING TO BE REDONE DUE TO THE DIMENSIONS OR GRADES SHOWN INCORRECTLY ON THESE PLANS, IF SUCH
NOTIFICATION HAS NOT BEEN GIVEN.

7.

8.

NO CHANGE IN DESIGN LOCATION OR GRADE WILL BE MADE BY THE CONTRACTOR WITHOUT THE WRITTEN APPROVAL OF THE
PROJECT ENGINEER.

CARE SHOULD BE TAKEN IN ALL EXCAVATIONS DUE TO POSSIBLE EXISTENCE OF UNRECORDED UTILITY LINES. EXCAVATION
REQUIRED WITHIN PROXIMITY OF EXISTING UTILITY LINES SHALL BE DONE BY HAND. CONTRACTOR SHALL REPAIR ANY
DAMAGE TO EXISTING UTILITY LINES OR STRUCTURES INCURRED DURING CONSTRUCTION OPERATIONS AT CONTRACTOR'S
EXPENSE.

4.

5.

6.

TRENCH BACKFILL MATERIAL AND COMPACTION TESTS ARE TO BE TAKEN PER APWA STANDARD SPECIFICATIONS (CURRENT
EDITION), SECTION 33 05 20 - BACKFILLING TRENCHES, OR AS REQUIRED BY THE GEOTECHNICAL REPORT IF NATIVE
MATERIALS ARE USED. NO NATIVE MATERIALS ARE ALLOWED IN THE PIPE ZONE. THE MAXIMUM LIFT FOR BACKFILLING
EXCAVATIONS IS DETERMINED BY THE GEOTECHNICAL RECOMMENDATIONS.
THE CONTRACTOR IS SOLELY RESPONSIBLE FOR CONFORMING TO LOCAL AND FEDERAL CODES GOVERNING SHORING AND
BRACING OF EXCAVATIONS AND TRENCHES AND FOR THE PROTECTION OF WORKERS.
THE CONTRACTOR IS REQUIRED TO KEEP ALL CONSTRUCTION ACTIVITIES WITHIN THE APPROVED PROJECT LIMITS. THIS
INCLUDES, BUT IS NOT LIMITED TO VEHICLE AND EQUIPMENT STAGING, MATERIAL STORAGE AND LIMITS OF TRENCH
EXCAVATION. IT IS THE CONTRACTOR'S RESPONSIBILITY TO OBTAIN PERMISSION AND/OR EASEMENTS FROM THE
APPROPRIATE GOVERNING ENTITY AND/OR INDIVIDUAL PROPERTY OWNER(S) FOR WORK OR STAGING OUTSIDE OF THE
PROJECT LIMITS.
THE CONTRACTOR IS RESPONSIBLE FOR REPAIRING ANY DAMAGE, CAUSED BY ANY CONDITION INCLUDING SETTLEMENT, TO
EXISTING UTILITIES FROM WORK PERFORMED AT OR NEAR EXISTING UTILITIES. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL TAKE ALL
MEASURES NECESSARY TO PROTECT ALL EXISTING PUBLIC AND PRIVATE ROADWAY AND UTILITY FACILITIES. DAMAGE TO
EXISTING FACILITIES CAUSED BY THE CONTRACTOR MUST BE REPAIRED BY THE CONTRACTOR AT HIS/HER EXPENSE TO THE
SATISFACTION OF THE OWNER OF SAID FACILITIES.

EXISTING STRIPING

THE CONTRACTOR SHALL REMOVE ALL ORGANIC MATERIAL AND OTHER DELETERIOUS MATERIALS PRIOR TO PLACING
GRADING FILL OR BASE COURSE. THE AREA SHOULD BE PROOF-ROLLED TO IDENTIFY ANY SOFT AREAS. WHERE SOFT
AREAS ARE ENCOUNTERED, THE CONTRACTOR SHALL REMOVE THE SOIL AND REPLACE WITH COMPACTED FILL.

CATCH BASIN, OR CLEANOUT BOX CONNECTIONS MUST BE MADE WITH THE PIPE CUT FLUSH WITH THE INSIDE OF THE BOX
AND GROUTED OR SEALED.

13.

NATURAL VEGETATION AND SOIL COVER SHALL NOT BE DISTURBED PRIOR TO ACTUAL CONSTRUCTION OF A REQUIRED FACILITY OR
IMPROVEMENT. MASS CLEARING OF THE SITE IN ANTICIPATION OF CONSTRUCTION SHALL BE AVOIDED.

EXISTING UTILITY INFORMATION SHOWN IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. IT IS DERIVED FROM ON-SITE SURVEY AND/OR
UTILITY MAPPING PROVIDED TO THE ENGINEER, AND THEREFORE UTILITIES MAY NOT BE LOCATED CORRECTLY, EITHER
HORIZONTALLY OR VERTICALLY, AND MAY NOT BE ALL INCLUSIVE. CONTRACTOR IS REQUIRED TO FOLLOW THE PROCEDURE
OUTLINED BELOW:
16.1.
CONTRACTOR IS REQUIRED TO LOCATE AND POTHOLE ALL EXISTING UTILITY LINES (BOTH HORIZONTALLY AND VERTICALLY)
THAT AFFECT THE PROJECT CONSTRUCTION, EITHER ON-SITE OR OFF-SITE, AND DETERMINE IF THERE ARE ANY CONFLICTS
WITH THE DESIGN OF THE SITE AS SHOWN ON THE APPROVED PLANS PRIOR TO ANY CONSTRUCTION. IF IT IS DETERMINED
THAT CONFLICTS EXIST BETWEEN EXISTING UTILITIES AND DESIGN UTILITIES (OR ANOTHER ASPECT OF PROPOSED
CONSTRUCTION) THE ENGINEER MUST BE NOTIFIED IMMEDIATELY TO CORRECT THE CONFLICTS BEFORE ANY WORK CAN BEGIN.
IF THE CONTRACTOR FAILS TO FOLLOW THIS ABSOLUTE REQUIREMENT AND CONFLICTS ARISE DURING CONSTRUCTION THE
CONTRACTOR WILL BEAR THE SOLE RESPONSIBILITY TO FIX THE CONFLICTS.
16.2.
CONTRACTOR IS REQUIRED TO VERIFY THAT PROPER COVER AND PROTECTION OF EXISTING UTILITY LINES IS MAINTAINED OR
ATTAINED WITHIN THE DESIGN ONCE VERIFICATION OF THE EXISTING UTILITIES IS COMPLETED AS OUTLINED IN 16.1 ABOVE.
16.3.
IN ADDITION TO 16.1 AND 16.2 ABOVE THE CONTRACTOR WILL VERIFY DEPTHS OF UTILITIES IN THE FIELD BY "POTHOLING" A
MINIMUM OF 300 FEET AHEAD OF PROPOSED PIPELINE CONSTRUCTION TO AVOID POTENTIAL CONFLICTS WITH DESIGNED
PIPELINE ALIGNMENT AND GRADE AND EXISTING UTILITIES.
16.4.
IF A CONFLICT ARISES BETWEEN EXISTING UTILITIES AND DESIGN UTILITIES (OR ANOTHER ASPECT OF PROPOSED
CONSTRUCTION) AS DETERMINED UNDER 16.1, 16.2 OR 16.3 THE CONTRACTOR WILL NOTIFY THE ENGINEER IMMEDIATELY TO
RESOLVE THE CONFLICT.
16.5.
IF A CONFLICT ARISES BETWEEN EXISTING UTILITIES AND DESIGN UTILITIES (OR ANOTHER ASPECT OF PROPOSED
CONSTRUCTION) RESULTING FROM THE CONTRACTOR'S NEGLIGENCE TO IDENTIFY AND/OR “POTHOLE” EXISTING UTILITIES AS
REQUIRED IN 16.1, 16.2 AND 16.3 ABOVE, THE CONTRACTOR WILL BE REQUIRED TO RESOLVE THE CONFLICT WITHOUT
ADDITIONAL COST OR CLAIM TO THE OWNER OR ENGINEER.

EXISTING UTILITIES HAVE BEEN SHOWN ON THE PLANS BASED ON ON-SITE SURVEY. PRIOR TO COMMENCING ANY WORK, IT
SHALL BE THE CONTRACTOR'S RESPONSIBILITY TO HAVE EACH UTILITY COMPANY LOCATE, IN THE FIELD, THEIR MAIN AND
SERVICE LINES. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL NOTIFY BLUE STAKES AT 1-800-662-4111 48 HOURS IN ADVANCE OF PERFORMING
ANY EXCAVATION WORK. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL RECORD THE BLUE STAKES ORDER NUMBER AND FURNISH ORDER
NUMBER TO OWNER AND ENGINEER PRIOR TO ANY EXCAVATION. IT WILL BE THE CONTRACTOR'S SOLE RESPONSIBILITY TO
DIRECTLY CONTACT ANY OTHER UTILITY COMPANIES THAT ARE NOT MEMBERS OF BLUE STAKES. IT SHALL BE THE
CONTRACTOR'S SOLE RESPONSIBILITY TO PROTECT ALL EXISTING UTILITIES SO THAT NO DAMAGE RESULTS TO THEM
DURING THE PERFORMANCE OF THIS CONTRACT. ANY REPAIRS NECESSARY TO DAMAGED UTILITIES SHALL BE PAID FOR BY
THE CONTRACTOR. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL BE REQUIRED TO COOPERATE WITH OTHER CONTRACTORS AND UTILITY
COMPANIES INSTALLING NEW STRUCTURES, UTILITIES AND SERVICE TO THE PROJECT.

4.

PERMITS, FEES AND AGREEMENTS
CONTRACTOR MUST OBTAIN ALL THE NECESSARY PERMITS AND AGREEMENTS AND PAY ALL
APPLICABLE FEES PRIOR TO ANY CONSTRUCTION ACTIVITIES. CONTACT SALT LAKE CITY
ENGINEERING (535-6248) FOR PERMITS AND INSPECTIONS REQUIRED FOR ANY WORK CONDUCTED
WITHIN SALT LAKE CITY'S PUBLIC RIGHT-OF-WAY. APPLICABLE UTILITY PERMITS MAY INCLUDE
MAINLINE EXTENSION AGREEMENTS AND SERVICE CONNECTION PERMITS. ALL UTILITY WORK MUST
BE BONDED. ALL CONTRACTORS MUST BE LICENSED TO WORK ON CITY UTILITY MAINS.
CONSTRUCTION SITES MUST BE IN COMPLIANCE WITH THE UTAH POLLUTION DISCHARGE ELIMINATION
SYSTEM (UPDES) STORM WATER PERMIT FOR CONSTRUCTION ACTIVITIES (538-6396). A COPY OF THE
PERMIT'S STORM WATER POLLUTION PREVENTION PLAN MUST BE SUBMITTED TO PUBLIC UTILITIES
FOR REVIEW AND APPROVAL. ADDITIONAL WATER QUALITY AND EROSION CONTROL MEASURES MAY
BE REQUIRED. THE CONTRACTOR MUST ALSO COMPLY WITH SALT LAKE CITY'S CLEAN WHEEL
ORDINANCE.

8.

TRAFFIC CONTROL AND HAUL ROUTES
TRAFFIC CONTROL MUST CONFORM TO THE MOST CURRENT EDITION OF SALT LAKE CITY TRAFFIC
CONTROL MANUAL - PART 6 OF “MANUAL ON UNIFORM TRAFFIC CONTROL DEVICES” FOR SALT LAKE
COUNTY AND STATE ROADS. SLC TRANSPORTATION MUST APPROVE ALL PROJECT HAUL ROUTES
(535-7129). THE CONTRACTOR MUST ALSO CONFORM TO UDOT, SALT LAKE COUNTY OR OTHER
APPLICABLE GOVERNING ENTITIES REQUIREMENTS FOR TRAFFIC CONTROL.
SURVEY CONTROL
CONTRACTOR MUST PROVDE A REGISTERED LAND SURVEYOR OR PERSONS UNDER SUPERVISION OF
A REGISTERED LAND SURVEYOR TO SET STAKES FOR ALIGNMENT AND GRADE OF EACH MAIN AND/OR
FACILITY AS APPROVED. THE STAKES SHALL BE MARKED WITH THE HORIZONTAL LOCATION (STATION)
AND VERTICAL LOCATION (GRADE) WITH CUTS AND/OR FILLS TO THE GRADE OF THE MAIN AND/OR
FACILITY AS APPROVED. IN ADDITION, THE CONTRACTOR AND/OR SURVEYOR SHALL PROVIDE TO SALT
LAKE CITY PUBLIC UTILITIES CUT SHEETS FILLED OUT COMPLETELY AND CLEARLY SHOWING THE
PERTINENT GRADES, ELEVATIONS AND CUT/FILLS ASSOCIATED WITH THE FIELD STAKING OF THE MAIN
AND/OR FACILITY. THE CUT SHEET FORM IS AVAILABLE AT THE CONTRACTS AND AGREEMENTS OFFICE
AT PUBLIC UTILITIES. ALL MAINS AND LATERALS NOT MEETING MINIMUM GRADE REQUIREMENTS AS
SPECIFIED BY ORDINANCE OR AS REQUIRED TO MEET THE MINIMUM REQUIRED FLOWS OR AS
APPROVED MUST BE REMOVED AND RECONSTRUCTED TO MEET DESIGN GRADE. THE CONTRACTOR
SHALL PROTECT ALL STAKES AND MARKERS UNTIL PUBLIC UTILITY SURVEYORS COMPLETE FINAL
MEASUREMENTS. THE CONTRACTOR WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR FURNISHING, MAINTAINING, OR
RESTORING ALL MONUMENTS AND REFERENCE MARKS WITHIN THE PROJECT SITE. CONTACT THE
COUNTY SURVEYOR (468-2028) FOR MONUMENT LOCATIONS AND CONSTRUCTION REQUIREMENTS.
ALL ELEVATIONS SHALL BE REFERENCED TO SALT LAKE CITY DATUM UNLESS NOTED OTHERWISE ON
THE PLANS.

10. SAFETY
THE CONTRACTOR IS RESPONSIBLE FOR ALL ASPECTS OF SAFETY OF THE PROJECT AND SHALL MEET
ALL OSHA, STATE, COUNTY AND OTHER GOVERNING ENTITY REQUIREMENTS.
THE CONTRACTOR IS SOLELY RESPONSIBLE FOR CONFORMING TO LOCAL AND FEDERAL CODES
GOVERNING SHORING AND BRACING OF EXCAVATIONS AND TRENCHES, AND FOR THE PROTECTION OF
WORKERS.
11. DUST CONTROL
THE CONTRACTOR IS RESPONSIBLE FOR DUST CONTROL ACCORDING TO THE GOVERNING ENTITY
STANDARDS. USE OF HYDRANT WATER OR PUMPING FROM CITY-OWNED CANALS OR STORM
DRAINAGE FACILITIES IS NOT ALLOWED FOR DUST CONTROL ACTIVITIES WITHOUT WRITTEN APPROVAL
OF THE PUBLIC UTILITIES DIRECTOR.
12. DEWATERING
ALL ON-SITE DEWATERING ACTIVITIES MUST BE APPROVED IN WRITING BY PUBLIC UTILITIES.
PROPOSED OUTFALL LOCATIONS AND ESTIMATED FLOW VOLUME CALCULATIONS MUST BE SUBMITTED
TO PUBLIC UTILITIES FOR REVIEW AND APPROVAL. ADEQUATE MEASURES MUST BE TAKEN TO
REMOVE ALL SEDIMENT PRIOR TO DISCHARGE. PUBLIC UTILITIES MAY REQUIRE ADDITIONAL
MEASURES FOR SEDIMENT CONTROL AND REMOVAL.

E. FIELD CHANGES NO ROADWAY, UTILITY ALIGNMENT OR GRADE CHANGES ARE ALLOWED FROM THE APPROVED
CONSTRUCTION PLANS/DOCUMENTS WITHOUT WRITTEN APPROVAL FROM THE SLC PUBLIC UTILITIES
DIRECTOR. CHANGES TO HYDRANT LOCATIONS AND/OR FIRE LINES MUST BE REVIEWED AND
APPROVED BY THE SALT LAKE CITY OR SALT LAKE COUNTY FIRE DEPARTMENT (AS APPLICABLE TO
THE PROJECT) AND PUBLIC UTILITIES.
F. PUBLIC NOTICE TO PROJECTS IN THE PUBLIC WAYFOR APPROVED PROJECTS THE CONTRACTOR IS RESPONSIBLE TO PROVIDE AND DISTRIBUTE
WRITTEN NOTICE TO ALL RESIDENTS LOCATED WITHIN THE PROJECT AREA AT LEAST 72-HOURS PRIOR
TO CONSTRUCTION. WORK TO BE CONDUCTED WITHIN COMMERCIAL OR INDUSTRIAL AREAS MAY
REQUIRE A LONGER NOTIFICATION PERIOD AND ADDITIONAL CONTRACTOR COORDINATION WITH
PROPERTY OWNERS. THE WRITTEN NOTICE IS TO BE APPROVED BY THE SLC PUBLIC UTILITIES
PROJECT ENGINEER.
G. PUBLIC NOTICE FOR WATER MAIN SHUT DOWNS THROUGH THE SLC PUBLIC UTILITIES INSPECTOR AND WITH THE PUBLIC UTILITIES PROJECT ENGINEER
APPROVAL, SLC PUBLIC UTILITIES MUST BE CONTACTED AND APPROVE ALL WATER MAIN SHUTDOWNS.
ONCE APPROVED THE CONTRACTOR MUST NOTIFY ALL EFFECTED USERS BY WRITTEN NOTICE A
MINIMUM OF 48-HOURS (RESIDENTIAL) AND 72-HOURS (COMMERCIAL/INDUSTRIAL) PRIOR TO THE
WATER MAIN SHUT DOWN. PUBLIC UTILITIES MAY REQUIRE LONGER NOTICE PERIODS.
H. WATER AND SEWER SEPARATION IN ACCORDANCE WITH UTAH'S DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH REGULATIONS, A MINIMUM TEN-FOOT
HORIZONTAL AND 1.5-FOOT VERTICAL (WITH WATER ON TOP) SEPARATION IS REQUIRED. IF THESE
CONDITIONS CANNOT BE MET, STATE AND SLC PUBLIC UTILITIES APPROVAL IS REQUIRED. ADDITIONAL
CONSTRUCTION MEASURES WILL BE REQUIRED FOR THESE CONDITIONS.
I. SALVAGE ALL METERS MUST BE RETURNED TO PUBLIC UTILITIES, AND AT PUBLIC UTILITIES REQUEST ALL
SALVAGED PIPE AND/OR FITTINGS MUST BE RETURNED TO SLC PUBLIC UTILTIES (483-6727) LOCATED
AT 1530 SOUTH WEST TEMPLE.
J. SEWER MAIN AND LATERAL CONSTRUCTION REQUIREMENTS SLC PUBLIC UTILITIES MUST APPROVE ALL SEWER CONNECTIONS. ALL SEWER LATERALS 6-INCHES
AND SMALLER MUST WYE INTO THE MAINS PER SLC PUBLIC UTILITIES REQUIREMENTS. ALL 8-INCH
AND LARGER SEWER CONNECTIONS MUST BE PETITIONED FOR AT PUBLIC UTILTIES (483-6762) AND
CONNECTED AT A MANHOLE. INSIDE DROPS IN MANHOLES ARE NOT ALLOWED. A MINIMUM 4-FOOT
BURY DEPTH IS REQUIRED ON ALL SEWER MAINS AND LATERALS. CONTRACTOR SHALL INSTALL
INVERT COVERS IN ALL SEWER MANHOLES WITHIN THE PROJECT AREA.
CONTRACTOR TO PROVIDE AIR PRESSURE TESTING OF SEWER MAINS IN ACCORDANCE WITH PIPE
MANUFACTURERS RECOMMENDATIONS AND SALT LAKE CITY PUBLIC UTILITIES REQUIREMENTS. ALL
PVC SEWER MAIN AND LATERAL TESTING SHALL BE IN ACCORDANCE WITH UNI-BELL UN-B-6-98
RECOMMENDED PRACTICE FOR LOW PRESSURE AIR TESTING OF INSTALLED SEWER PIPE.
CONTRACTOR SHALL PROVIDE SEWER LATERAL WATER TESTING AS REQUIRED BY THE SALT LAKE
CITY PUBLIC UTILITIES PROJECT ENGINEER OR INSPECTOR. A MINIMUM OF 9-FEET OF HEAD
PRESSURE IS REQUIRED AS MEASURED VERTICALLY FROM THE HIGH POINT OF THE PIPELINE AND AT
OTHER LOCATIONS ALONG THE PIPELINE AS DETERMINED BY THE SLC PUBLIC UTILITIES PROJECT
ENGINEER OR INSPECTOR. TESTING TIME WILL BE NO LESS THAN AS SPECIFIED FOR THE AIR TEST
DURATION IN TABLE I ON PAGE 12 OF UNI-B-6-98. ALL PIPES SUBJECT TO WATER TESTING SHALL BE
FULLY VISIBLE TO THE INSPECTOR DURING TESTING. TESTING MUST BE PERFORMED IN THE
PRESENCE OF A SLC PUBLIC UTILITIES REPRESENTATIVE. ALL VISIBLE LEAKAGE MUST BE REPAIRED
TO THE SATISFACTION OF THE SLC PUBLIC UTILITIES ENGINEER OR INSPECTOR.
K. WATER AND FIRE MAIN AND SERVICE CONSTRUCTION REQUIREMENTS SLC PUBLIC UTILITIES MUST APPROVE ALL FIRE AND WATER SERVICE CONNECTIONS. A MINIMUM
3-FOOT SEPARATION IS REQUIRED BETWEEN ALL WATER AND FIRE SERVICE TAPS INTO THE MAIN. ALL
CONNECTIONS MUST BE MADE MEETING SLC PUBLIC UTILITIES REQUIREMENTS. A 5-FOOT MINIMUM
BURY DEPTH (FINAL GRADE TO TOP OF PIPE) IS REQUIRED ON ALL WATER/FIRE LINES UNLESS
OTHERWISE APPROVED BY PUBLIC UTILITIES. WATER LINE THRUST BLOCK AND RESTRAINTS ARE AS
PER SLC APPROVED DETAIL DRAWINGS AND SPECIFICATIONS. ALL EXPOSED NUTS AND BOLTS WILL
BE COATED WITH CHEVRON FM1 GREASE PLUS MINIMUM 8 MIL THICKNESS PLASTIC. PROVIDE
STAINLESS STEEL NUTS, BOLTS AND WASHERS FOR HIGH GROUNDWATER/ SATURATED CONDITIONS
AT FLANGE FITTINGS, ETC.
ALL WATERLINES INSTALLATIONS AND TESTING TO BE IN ACCORDANCE WITH AWWA SECTIONS C600,
C601, C651, C206, C200, C900, C303 AWWA MANUAL M11 AND ALL OTHER APPLICABLE AWWA, UPWS,
ASTM AND ANSI SPECIFICATIONS RELEVANT TO THE INSTALLATION AND COMPLETION OF THE
PROJECT. AMENDMENT TO SECTION C600 SECTION 4.1.1; DOCUMENT TO READ MINIMUM TEST
PRESSURE SHALL NOT BE LESS THAN 200 P.S.I. GAUGED TO A HIGH POINT OF THE PIPELINE BEING
TESTED. ALL MATERIALS USED FOR WATERWORKS PROJECTS TO BE RATED FOR 150 P.S.I. MINIMUM
OPERATING PRESSURE.

TEMPORARY ASPHALT
IF THE CONTRACTOR CHOOSES TO WORK WITHIN THE PUBLIC WAY WHEN HOT MIX ASPHALT IS NOT
AVAILABLE, THE CONTRACTOR MUST OBTAIN APPROVAL FROM THE APPROPRIATE GOVERNING ENTITY
PRIOR TO INSTALLING TEMPORARY ASPHALT SURFACING MATERIAL. WITHIN SALT LAKE CITY, WHEN
PERMANENT ASPHALT BECOMES AVAILABLE, THE CONTRACTOR SHALL REMOVE THE TEMPORARY
ASPHALT, FURNISH AND INSTALL THE PERMANENT ASPHALT. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL GUARANTEE
THE ASPHALT RESTORATION FOR A PERIOD AS REQUIRED BY THE GOVERNING ENTITY FROM THE
DATE OF COMPLETION.

D. UTILITY RELOCATIONS FOR UTILITY CONFLICTS REQUIRING MAINLINE RELOCATIONS, THE CONTRACTOR MUST NOTIFY THE
APPLICABLE UTILITY COMPANY OR USER A MINIMUM OF 2-WEEKS IN ADVANCE. A ONE-WEEK MINIMUM
NOTIFICATION IS REQUIRED FOR CONFLICTS REQUIRING THE RELOCATION OF SERVICE LATERALS.
ALL RELOCATIONS ARE SUBJECT TO APPROVAL FROM THE APPLICABLE UTILITY COMPANY AND/OR
USER.

CONTRACTOR IS TO INSTALL WATER SERVICE LINES, METER YOKES AND/OR ASSEMBLIES AND METER
BOXS WITH LIDS LOCATED AS APPROVED ON THE PLANS PER APPLICABLE PUBLIC UTILITIES DETAIL
DRAWINGS. METER BOXES ARE TO BE PLACED IN THE PARK STRIPS PERPENDICULAR TO THE
WATERMAIN SERVICE TAP CONNECTION. ALL WATER METERS, CATCH BASINS, CLEANOUT BOXES,
MANHOLES, DOUBLE CHECK VALVE DETECTOR ASSEMBLIES, REDUCED PRESSURE DETECTOR
ASSEMBLIES AND BACKFLOW PREVENTION DEVICES MUST BE LOCATED OUTSIDE OF ALL
APPROACHES, DRIVEWAYS, PEDESTRIAN WALKWAYS AND OTHER TRAVELED WAYS UNLESS
OTHERWISE APPROVED ON PLANS.
BACKFLOW PREVENTORS ARE REQUIRED ON ALL IRRIGATION AND FIRE SPRINKLING TAPS PER PUBLIC
UTILITIES AND SLC FIRE DEPARTMENT REQUIREMENTS. CONTRACTORS SHALL INSTALL BACKFLOW
PREVENTION DEVICES ON FIRE SPRINKLER CONNECTIONS. DOUBLE CHECK VALVE ASSEMBLIES SHALL
BE INSTALLED ON CLASS 1, 2 AND 3 SYSTEMS. REDUCED PRESSURE PRINCIPLE VALVES SHALL BE
INSTALLED ON CLASS 4 SYSTEMS. ALL FIRE SPRINKLING BACKFLOW ASSEMBLIES SHALL CONFORM TO
ASSE STANDARD 1048, 1013, 1047 AND 1015. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL BE RESPONSIBLE TO PERFORM
BACKFLOW PREVENTION TESTS PER SALT LAKE CITY STANDARDS AND SUBMIT RESULTS TO PUBLIC
UTILITIES. ALL TESTS MUST BE PERFORMED AND SUBMITTED TO PUBLIC UTILITIES WITHIN 10 DAYS OF
INSTALLATION OR WATER TURN-ON. BACKFLOW TEST FORMS ARE AVAILABLE AT PUBLIC UTILITIES'
CONTRACTS AND AGREEMENTS OFFICE.

TO THE PROJECT. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL GUARANTEE THE ASPHALT RESTORATION FOR A PERIOD
AS REQUIRED BY THE GOVERNING ENTITY.

C. UTILITY LOCATIONS CONTRACTOR WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR LOCATING AND AVOIDING ALL UTILITIES AND SERVICE
LATERALS, AND FOR REPAIRING ALL DAMAGE THAT OCCURS TO THE UTILTIES DUE TO THE
CONTRACTOR'S ACTIVITIES. CONTRACTOR IS TO VERIFY LOCATION, DEPTH, SIZE, MATERIAL AND
OUTSIDE DIAMETERS OF UTILITIES IN THE FIELD BY POTHOLING A MINIMUM OF 300-FEET AHEAD OF
SCHEDULED CONSTRUCTION IN ORDER TO IDENTIFY POTENTIAL CONFLICTS AND PROBLEMS WITH

UTILITIES' MAPS MUST BE ASSUMED AS APPROXIMATE AND REQUIRING FIELD VERIFICATION.
CONTACT BLUE STAKES OR APPROPRIATE OWNER FOR COMMUNICATION LINE LOCATIONS.

9.

ASPHALT AND SOIL TESTING
THE CONTRACTOR IS TO PROVIDE MARSHALL AND PROCTOR TEST DATA 24-HOURS PRIOR TO USE.
CONTRACTOR IS TO PROVIDE COMPACTION AND DENSITY TESTING AS REQUIRED BY SALT LAKE CITY
ENGINEERING, UDOT, SALT LAKE COUNTY OR OTHER GOVERNING ENTITY. TRENCH BACKFILL
MATERIAL AND COMPACTION TESTS ARE TO BE TAKEN PER APWA STANDARD SPECIFICATIONS,
SECTION 330520 - BACKFILLING TRENCHES, OR AS REQUIRED BY THE SLC PROJECT ENGINEER IF
NATIVE MATERIALS ARE USED. NO NATIVE MATERIALS ARE ALLOWED WITHIN THE PIPE ZONE. THE
MAXIMUM LIFTS FOR BACKFILLING EXCAVATIONS IS 8-INCHES. ALL MATERIALS AND COMPACTION
TESTING IS TO BE PERFORMED BY A LAB RECOGNIZED AND ACCEPTED BY SALT LAKE COUNTY PUBLIC
WORKS AND/OR SALT LAKE CITY ENGINEERING.

B. DAMAGE TO EXISTING UTILITIES THE CONTRACTOR IS RESPONSIBLE FOR REPAIRING ANY DAMAGE, CAUSED BY ANY CONDITION
INCLUDING SETTLEMENT, TO EXISTING UTILITIES FROM WORK PERFORMED AT OR NEAR EXISTING
UTILITIES. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL TAKE ALL MEASURES NECESSARY TO PROTECT ALL EXISTING
PUBLIC AND PRIVATE ROADWAY AND UTILITY FACILITIES. DAMAGE TO EXISTING FACILITIES CAUSED
BY THE CONTRACTOR, MUST BE REPAIRED BY THE CONTRACTOR AT HIS/HER EXPENSE, TO THE
SATISFACTION OF THE OWNER OF SAID FACILITIES.

ALL MANHOLES, HYDRANTS, VALVES, CLEAN-OUT BOXES, CATCH BASINS, METERS, ETC. MUST BE
RAISED OR LOWERED TO FINAL GRADE PER PUBLIC UTILITIES STANDARDS AND INSPECTOR
REQUIREMENTS. CONCRETE COLLARS MUST BE CONSTRUCTED ON ALL MANHOLES, CLEANOUT
BOXES, CATCH BASINS AND VALVES PER PUBLIC UTILITIES STANDARDS. ALL MANHOLE, CATCH BASIN,
OR CLEANOUT BOX CONNECTIONS MUST BE MADE WITH THE PIPE CUT FLUSH WITH THE INSIDE OF THE
BOX AND GROUTED OR SEALED AS REQUIRED BY THE PUBLIC UTILITIES INSPECTOR. ALL MANHOLE,
CLEANOUT BOX OR CATCH BASIN DISCONNECTIONS MUST BE REPAIRED AND GROUTED AS REQUIRED
BY THE ON-SITE PUBLIC UTILITIES INSPECTOR.

GENERAL NOTES
THIS PLAN IS DESIGNED AS A FIRST APPRAISAL OF NECESSARY MEANS TO PROTECT THE WATERS OF THE
STATE FROM POTENTIAL POLLUTION. IT IS THE RESPONSIBILITY OF THE OWNER/OPERATOR TO ADD
WARRANTED BEST MANAGEMENT PRACTICES (BMP'S) AS NECESSARY, MODIFY THOSE SHOWN AS
APPROPRIATE, AND DELETE FROM THE PROJECT THOSE FOUND TO BE UNNECESSARY. FEDERAL AND STATE
LAW ALLOWS THESE UPDATES TO BE MADE BY THE OWNER/OPERATOR ONSITE AND RECORDED BY THE
OWNER/OPERATOR ON THE COPY OF THE SWPPP KEPT ONSITE.
DISTURBED LAND SHALL BE KEPT TO A MINIMUM. STABILIZATION MEASURES SHALL BE INITIATED AS SOON AS
PRACTICABLE IN PORTIONS OF THE SITE WHERE CONSTRUCTION ACTIVITIES HAVE TEMPORARILY OR
PERMANENTLY CEASED, BUT IN NO CASE MORE THAN 14 DAYS AFTER THE CONSTRUCTION ACTIVITY IN THAT
PORTION OF THE SITE HAS TEMPORARILY OR PERMANENTLY CEASED. HOWEVER, WHERE CONSTRUCTION
ACTIVITY ON A PORTION OF THE SITE IS TEMPORARILY CEASED, AND EARTH DISTURBING ACTIVITIES WILL BE
RESUMED WITHIN 21 DAYS, TEMPORARY STABILIZATION MEASURES DO NOT HAVE TO BE INITIATED ON THAT
PORTION OF THE SITE.

C-500

Proposed Three-Lot Residential Subdivision
2193 E. 6525 S. Cottonwood Heights, Utah
Written Narrative
1. Overall Rationale and Intent of the Project
The purpose of this application is to subdivide an existing 1.08-acre residential property into
three single-family residential lots. The proposed subdivision is intended to provide thoughtfully
designed homesites that are compatible with the surrounding neighborhood while making
efficient use of existing infrastructure and public utilities.
The project represents an example of sensitive infill development by utilizing an existing
residential parcel located within an established neighborhood. Rather than extending
development into previously undeveloped areas, the proposal increases housing opportunities
within an area already served by public streets, water, sanitary sewer, storm drainage, natural
gas, electricity, and other municipal services.
Each proposed lot will contain approximately 15,500-15,700 square feet, providing generous
building sites with over 95 feet of frontage and an average depth of approximately 165 feet. The
resulting lots will maintain the spacious residential character of the neighborhood while
providing additional homeownership opportunities that reflect current housing demand in
Cottonwood Heights.
The subdivision has been designed to preserve neighborhood aesthetics through quality
residential development, maintain adequate setbacks, provide safe access, and utilize existing
public infrastructure without requiring new public streets. Because the lots are comparable in
size to many surrounding residential parcels, the development remains consistent with the area's
established low-density residential character.

2. Consistency with the Cottonwood Heights General Plan, Zoning Ordinance,
and Applicable Planning Documents
The proposed subdivision supports several objectives identified within the Cottonwood Heights
General Plan by encouraging well-designed infill residential development where adequate
infrastructure already exists.
Specifically, the project:
•
•
•

Promotes efficient use of existing public infrastructure and utilities.
Encourages orderly residential growth within developed neighborhoods.
Increases housing opportunities while maintaining neighborhood compatibility.

•
•

Preserves the residential character through generous lot sizes and low-density
development.
Utilizes existing public transportation without requiring infrastructure improvements.

The proposed lots exceed the minimum lot size requirements of the requested zoning designation
and have been configured to provide functional building envelopes, appropriate setbacks, and
sufficient frontage for attractive single-family homes.
Because the subdivision occurs entirely within an existing residential neighborhood and does not
introduce commercial or higher-intensity uses, the proposal maintains consistency with the longterm vision established by the City's planning policies for stable residential neighborhoods.
The project also complements surrounding development patterns by creating lots that remain
significantly larger than many existing residential lots throughout Cottonwood Heights while
making efficient use of underutilized land.

3. Property Size
Gross Site Area
•
•

Approximately 1.08 acres
Approximately 47,045 square feet

Street Right-of-Way Dedication
•

Approximately 3450 square feet (to be finalized by survey and engineering).
o Public utility easement, curb/gutter and sidewalk.
o South frontage of property measuring approximately 288x12 feet.

Net Developable Area
•

Approximately 0 square feet following any required dedication.

The subdivision utilizes the existing public street system and does not require construction of
new public roadways.

4. Number of Dwelling Units and Density
The proposed subdivision will create:
•
•

Three (3) residential lots
Three (3) single-family detached dwelling units

Overall residential density:
•

Approximately 2.78 dwelling units per acre

This density remains consistent with low-density residential development and reflects an
appropriate transition within the surrounding neighborhood.

5. Proposed Land Use Classification
Primary Use
•
•

Single-family detached residential dwellings (Permitted)

Accessory Uses
Typical accessory residential uses permitted by the Cottonwood Heights Zoning Ordinance,
including but not limited to:
•

Home occupations where permitted by ordinance.

No conditional or commercial land uses are proposed as part of this subdivision.

Because each lot exceeds 15,000 square feet, substantial private open space will be provided on
every parcel, eliminating the need for separate common open space facilities while maintaining
the open residential character of the neighborhood.

Summary
This subdivision represents a carefully planned residential infill project that creates three
generously sized single-family lots while preserving the established character of the surrounding
neighborhood. The proposal efficiently utilizes existing infrastructure, supports the goals of the
Cottonwood Heights General Plan, provides additional housing opportunities, and results in a
high-quality residential development that will be a positive contribution to the community.

COTTONWOOD HEIGHTS CITY
PLANNING COMMISSION
STAFF REPORT
October 21, 2026
Summary
Project Number:
SUB-26-007
Subject Properties:
2196 E. 6450 S
Action Requested:
Plat Amendment
Applicant:
Jordan and Brooke Brady
Recommendation:
APPROVE WITH
CONDITIONS

Context
Property Owner:
BRADY FAM TRUST
Acreage:
Approx. 1.11 acre

Request
The applicant requests approval of a subdivision plat amendment to amend all of Lot 15 and a portion of
Lot 14 of the Ellison Woods Subdivision and establish the North Brady Subdivision, consisting of two singlefamily residential lots.
The proposed subdivision would establish Lot 101 at approximately 30,217 square feet (0.694 acres) and
Lot 102 as an additional residential building lot. The proposal would retain the existing single-family
residence on Lot 101 and create one additional lot for future residential development.
The proposed subdivision remains subject to completion of applicable City and agency technical reviews
prior to final plat approval and recordation.

Planning Commission – October 21, 2026
Project SUB-26-007 – 2196 E. 6450 S.

Background & Context
The subject property is located along 6450 South within an established single-family
residential neighborhood. The property contains an existing single-family residence and
associated residential improvements.
The applicant previously requested a General Plan Land Use Map Amendment and Zoning
Map Amendment to change the property from Residential – Rural Density and RR-1-21
zoning to Residential – Low Density and R-1-15 zoning. The purpose of those requests was
to facilitate a future two-lot residential subdivision.
The proposed North Brady Subdivision is consistent with the residential infill concept
presented with the earlier land use amendment applications. However, subdivision
approval is a separate land use action requiring compliance with applicable zoning,
subdivision, engineering, and utility standards.
The September 22, 2026 subdivision plans identify the proposed lot boundaries, existing
structures, utility infrastructure, access improvements, easements, grading, and
stormwater facilities.

Review Status
The North Brady Subdivision is currently undergoing technical review by City staff and
applicable reviewing agencies. Water, sewer, and Fire Department reviews have been
completed and approved. Based on the initial review, staff has not identified any major
land-use or subdivision-design issues that would prevent the application from proceeding
to the Planning Commission for consideration.
Several remaining technical and drafting items are still under review and may require
revisions to the subdivision plat and associated construction documents.
Based on the review completed to date, staff does not anticipate that resolution of the
remaining comments will materially alter the basic subdivision design presented to the
Planning Commission, including the proposed two-lot configuration, general lot
boundaries, lot areas, or frontage. Any revisions that would result in a material change to the
subdivision design would be subject to additional City review, as applicable.
Planning Commission approval of the subdivision plat amendment would therefore be
subject to the applicant satisfactorily addressing all remaining staff and agency review
comments prior to final plat approval, City signatures, and recordation.

Page 2 of 6

Planning Commission – October 21, 2026
Project SUB-26-007 – 2196 E. 6450 S.

Analysis & Findings
Land Use and Zoning
The proposed subdivision would establish two lots intended for detached single-family residential
use.
The proposed plat identifies Lot 101 at approximately 30,217 square feet, exceeding the 15,000square-foot minimum lot area associated with the R-1-15 zoning district. Lot 102 is proposed as the
additional residential building lot.
Staff Analysis: The proposed two-lot configuration is consistent with the residential infill concept
previously presented to the City. Final verification of both lots' areas, widths, frontage, setbacks, and
other dimensional requirements is required before recordation.
Plat Amendment
The proposed North Brady Subdivision would amend all of Lot 15 and a portion of Lot 14 of the
recorded Ellison Woods Subdivision.
The amendment would establish Lots 101 and 102 and identify applicable property boundaries,
dedications, and easements.
Staff Analysis: The proposed amendment would create one additional residential building lot while
retaining the existing residence. The final plat must accurately identify the affected recorded lots,
legal descriptions, existing easements, and any necessary easement modifications.
Access and Frontage Improvements
The proposed subdivision is located along 6450 South, an existing public roadway. The submitted
civil plans identify a proposed 20-foot-wide asphalt driveway and fire access serving the
development.
Staff Analysis: The proposed access arrangement must be reviewed for compliance with applicable
driveway, emergency access, frontage, and public improvement standards. Final access geometry
and improvements remain subject to Public Works and Fire Department review.
Utilities
The submitted construction plans identify existing water, sanitary sewer, gas, power, and other utility
infrastructure in the vicinity of the project and propose utility service connections for the two lots.
Staff Analysis - Water and sewer reviews have been completed and approved. Other applicable
utility and City technical requirements shall be addressed prior to final plat approval, recordation,
and/or construction authorization, as applicable.
Easements
The survey and proposed subdivision materials identify existing utility, sewer, and drainage
easements affecting the property.

Page 3 of 6

Planning Commission – October 21, 2026
Project SUB-26-007 – 2196 E. 6450 S.
Staff Analysis: Existing easements must be accurately reflected on the amended plat. Any
easement proposed for relocation, modification, or vacation shall be appropriately documented and
approved before recordation.
Drainage and Stormwater
The submitted drainage plans propose individual onsite stormwater retention facilities for both
lots.
The plans identify the following preliminary retention volumes:
•

Lot 101: 445 cubic feet required; 496 cubic feet provided.

•

Lot 102: 358 cubic feet required; 373 cubic feet provided.

Staff Analysis: The proposed retention facilities provide storage volumes exceeding the calculated
requirements shown in the submitted plans. Final grading, stormwater calculations, dry-well
design, and erosion-control measures remain subject to City Engineer review and approval

Page 4 of 6

Planning Commission – October 21, 2026
Project SUB-26-007 – 2196 E. 6450 S.

Subdivision Amendment Procedure
12.26.010 Plat Vacation Process

A. The planning commission may, with or without a petition, consider any proposed vacation,
alteration, or amendment of a subdivision plat, any portion of a subdivision plat, or any
street, lot, or alley contained in a subdivision plat at a public hearing.
B. If a petition is filed, the planning commission shall hold a public hearing within 45 days after
receipt of a petition.

12.26.020 Notice Of Hearing For Plat Change
A. The planning commission shall cause notice of the proposed plat change to be mailed to
each owner of real property located within 400 feet of the property that is the subject of the
proposed plat change, addressed to the owner’s mailing address appearing on the most
recent assessment rolls of the Salt Lake County Assessor.
B. The notice shall include the date, place, and time when the hearing will be held to consider
such proposed plat change.
C. If the proposed change involves the vacation, alteration, or amendment of a street, the
planning commission shall also cause notice of the date, place, and time of the hearing
regarding the matter to be given as required by UTAH CODE ANN. § 10-9a-609.5, as
amended.

Recommendation
Based on the submitted subdivision plat and supporting civil plans, staff finds that the proposed
North Brady Subdivision is generally consistent with city standards.
Staff recommends that the Planning Commission APPROVE WITH CONDITIONS the North Brady
Subdivision plat amendment, subject to completion of the remaining City technical review process
and resolution of outstanding comments prior to final plat approval and recordation.
Conditions of Approval
1. Technical Review. The applicant shall address all remaining comments from Planning,
Engineering, Public Works, Fire, utility providers, and other applicable reviewing agencies
prior to final plat approval and recordation.
2. Zoning Compliance. The final plat shall demonstrate compliance with the applicable zoning
district, including lot area, width, frontage, setbacks, and other dimensional requirements.
3. Engineering and Public Improvements. Final access, frontage improvements, grading,
drainage, stormwater facilities, and other public improvements shall be reviewed and
approved by the City Engineer and applicable agencies, prior to final approval and
recordation.
4. Easements and Title. All existing and proposed easements, legal descriptions, dedications,
and title interests shall be verified and appropriately reflected on the final plat. Any required
easement modifications shall be completed before recordation.
Page 5 of 6

Planning Commission – October 21, 2026
Project SUB-26-007 – 2196 E. 6450 S.
5. Utility and Fire Approvals. The applicant shall obtain all required utility-provider and Fire
Department approvals, including approval of the proposed driveway and emergency access
arrangements.
6. Final Plat Compliance. The final plat shall incorporate all required corrections and comply
with applicable subdivision, zoning, engineering, and recording requirements.
7. Recordation. The final plat shall be recorded within the applicable approval period
established by City Code unless an extension is approved in accordance with applicable
requirements.

Page 6 of 6

Proposed Two-Lot Residential Subdivision
2196 E. 6450 S. Cottonwood Heights, Utah
Written Narrative
1. Overall Rationale and Intent of the Project
The purpose of this application is to subdivide an existing 1.11-acre residential property into two
single-family residential lots. The proposed subdivision is intended to provide an additional
thoughtfully designed homesite that is compatible with the surrounding neighborhood while
making efficient use of existing infrastructure and public utilities.
The project represents an example of sensitive infill development by utilizing an existing
residential parcel located within an established neighborhood. Rather than extending
development into previously undeveloped areas, the proposal increases housing opportunities
within an area already served by public streets, water, sanitary sewer, storm drainage, natural
gas, electricity, and other municipal services.
Each proposed lot will be approximately 18,900 for the new development lot and 29,850 square
feet for the existing residence lot. The resulting lots will maintain the spacious residential
character of the neighborhood while providing additional homeownership opportunities that
reflect current housing demand in Cottonwood Heights.
The subdivision has been designed to preserve and improve neighborhood aesthetics through
quality residential development, maintain adequate setbacks, provide safe access, and utilize
existing public infrastructure without requiring new public streets. Because the lots are
comparable in size to many surrounding residential parcels, the development remains consistent
with the area's established low-density residential character.

2. Consistency with the Cottonwood Heights General Plan, Zoning Ordinance,
and Applicable Planning Documents
The proposed subdivision supports several objectives identified within the Cottonwood Heights
General Plan by encouraging well-designed infill residential development where adequate
infrastructure already exists.
Specifically, the project:
•
•
•
•

Promotes efficient use of existing public infrastructure and utilities.
Encourages orderly residential growth within developed neighborhoods.
Increases housing opportunities while maintaining neighborhood compatibility.
Preserves the residential character through generous lot sizes and low-density
development.

•

Utilizes existing public transportation without requiring infrastructure improvements.

The proposed lots exceed the minimum lot size requirements of the requested zoning designation
and have been configured to provide functional building envelopes, appropriate setbacks, and
sufficient frontage for attractive single-family homes.
Because the subdivision occurs entirely within an existing residential neighborhood and does not
introduce commercial or higher intensity uses, the proposal maintains consistency with the longterm vision established by the City's planning policies for stable residential neighborhoods.
The project also complements surrounding development patterns by creating lots that remain
significantly larger than many existing residential lots throughout Cottonwood Heights while
making efficient use of underutilized land.

3. Property Size
Gross Site Area

Summary
This subdivision represents a carefully planned residential infill project that creates two
generously sized single-family lots while preserving the established character of the surrounding
neighborhood. The proposal efficiently utilizes existing infrastructure, supports the goals of the
Cottonwood Heights General Plan, provides additional housing opportunities, and results in a
high-quality residential development that will be a positive contribution to the community.

NOTICE TO CONTRACTOR

NOTICE TO DEVELOPER/ CONTRACTOR

ALL CONTRACTORS AND SUBCONTRACTORS PERFORMING WORK SHOWN ON OR RELATED TO THESE PLANS SHALL
CONDUCT THEIR OPERATIONS SO THAT ALL EMPLOYEES ARE PROVIDED A SAFE PLACE TO WORK AND THE PUBLIC IS
PROTECTED. ALL CONTRACTORS AND SUBCONTRACTORS SHALL COMPLY WITH THE "OCCUPATIONAL SAFETY AND HEALTH
REGULATIONS OF THE U.S. DEPARTMENT OF LABOR AND THE STATE OF UTAH DEPARTMENT OF INDUSTRIAL RELATIONS
CONSTRUCTION SAFETY ORDERS." THE CIVIL ENGINEER SHALL NOT BE RESPONSIBLE IN ANY WAY FOR THE CONTRACTORS
AND SUBCONTRACTORS COMPLIANCE WITH SAID REGULATIONS AND ORDERS.

UNAPPROVED DRAWINGS REPRESENT WORK IN PROGRESS, ARE SUBJECT TO CHANGE, AND DO NOT CONSTITUTE A
FINISHED ENGINEERING PRODUCT. ANY WORK UNDERTAKEN BY DEVELOPER OR CONTRACTOR BEFORE PLANS ARE
APPROVED IS UNDERTAKEN AT THE SOLE RISK OF THE DEVELOPER, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO BIDS, ESTIMATION,
FINANCING, BONDING, SITE CLEARING, GRADING, INFRASTRUCTURE CONSTRUCTION, ETC.

CONTRACTOR FURTHER AGREES TO ASSUME SOLE AND COMPLETE RESPONSIBILITY FOR JOB-SITE CONDITIONS DURING
THE COURSE OF CONSTRUCTION OF THIS PROJECT, INCLUDING SAFETY OF ALL PERSONS AND PROPERTY, THAT THIS
REQUIREMENT SHALL APPLY CONTINUOUSLY AND NOT BE LIMITED TO NORMAL WORKING HOURS, AND THAT THE
CONTRACTOR SHALL DEFEND, INDEMNIFY AND HOLD THE OWNER AND THE CIVIL ENGINEER HARMLESS FROM ANY AND ALL
LIABILITY, REAL OR ALLEGED IN CONNECTION WITH THE PERFORMANCE OF WORK ON THIS PROJECT, EXCEPTING FOR
LIABILITY ARISING FROM THE SOLE NEGLIGENCE OF THE OWNER OR ENGINEER.

13.

NATURAL VEGETATION AND SOIL COVER SHALL NOT BE DISTURBED PRIOR TO ACTUAL CONSTRUCTION OF A REQUIRED FACILITY OR
